message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering the 24-hour window ending 2026-07-10 05:10 IST (2026-07-09 23:40 UTC). Relevant new items were confirmed for Microsoft Edge and Ubuntu-packaged components, including Python on Ubuntu. I did not find confirmed new MongoDB-family, FortiOS/FortiGate, SonicWall, Cisco Nexus/UCS/Fabric Extender, VMware ESXi/vCenter/Tools, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, OpenSSL, Apache Tomcat, Nginx, Firefox, or Chrome stable advisories newly published within this window.

**Finding 1**

- Product: Microsoft Edge
- Issue: July 09, 2026 Microsoft Edge Stable security update; CVE identifiers pending in the Microsoft release note.
- Severity: Not clearly stated.
- Description: Microsoft released Edge Stable version 150.0.4078.65, stating that it incorporates the latest Chromium security updates. The same release note says CVEs will be added when available.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored product list includes Microsoft Edge, and the source is Microsoft's Edge security release notes.
- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnotes-security

**Finding 2**

- Product: Ubuntu / Python packages on Ubuntu 16.04 LTS
- Issue: CVE-2026-7210 / USN-8524-1
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Ubuntu.
- Description: Ubuntu reports that Python could be made to crash via specially crafted input because Python did not use sufficient entropy for Expat hash-flooding protection in XML parsing modules.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored product list includes both Ubuntu and Python. The notice applies to Ubuntu 16.04 LTS Python packages.
- Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8524-1

**Finding 3**

- Product: Ubuntu / Linux kernel for Raspberry Pi systems
- Issue: USN-8492-4 and USN-8490-2 Linux kernel vulnerability updates
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Ubuntu.
- Description: Ubuntu published Raspberry Pi kernel updates for Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and 25.10, covering numerous Linux kernel flaws. Ubuntu states that attackers could possibly use the issues to compromise the system.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored product list includes Ubuntu. This applies specifically to Ubuntu Raspberry Pi kernel deployments.
- Sources: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8492-4 and https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8490-2

**Finding 4**

- Product: Ubuntu / curl package
- Issue: USN-8525-1, including CVE-2026-10536, CVE-2026-5545, CVE-2026-5773, CVE-2026-7168, CVE-2026-12064, CVE-2026-11586, CVE-2026-11352, CVE-2026-11564, and older CVEs carried in the update
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Ubuntu.
- Description: Ubuntu fixed several curl issues involving credential exposure, denial of service, possible arbitrary code execution, SSH host verification handling, and other connection-handling problems across supported and Pro-supported Ubuntu releases.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored product list includes Ubuntu; curl is an official Ubuntu package commonly present on monitored servers.
- Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8525-1

**Finding 5**

- Product: Ubuntu package set
- Issue: USN-8526-1 libheif, USN-8523-1 libsoup, USN-8522-1 LibRaw, USN-8521-1 Libidn, USN-8520-1 Expat, and USN-8519-1 Go Cryptography
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Ubuntu.
- Description: Ubuntu published multiple package updates on 9 July 2026 addressing denial of service, information exposure, and related parsing or cryptographic handling flaws in official Ubuntu packages.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored product list includes Ubuntu. These notices apply only where the affected packages are installed.
- Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices

**Possible matches needing review**

- Google Chrome: Google published a Chrome stable security update dated 8 July 2026 with 27 fixes, including critical and high-severity CVEs, but the source date falls outside the current scheduled run's July 9 to July 10 IST window. I excluded it from confirmed findings for this run unless your intended window is broader than the scheduled 24 hours.
- MongoDB family: I searched MongoDB server, mongod, mongos, Atlas, Ops Manager, drivers, connectors, and GitHub/NVD-style advisory terms. I did not find a credible new MongoDB-family vulnerability in the current 24-hour window.

Closing note: Review is recommended for Edge update status and Ubuntu hosts, especially systems running affected Python, curl, Raspberry Pi kernel, or listed library packages. Severity was not clearly stated for the Ubuntu notices, and Microsoft had not yet populated CVE details for the Edge release at the time of this sweep.
